answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring every identity to anchor a refundable stake to one verified kernel of reputation: a small deposit locked in shared escrow, forfeited on proven misbehavior. New agents must also earn nectar, slow non-transferable reputation points granted only for work peers attest as useful, before transacting at full volume. A sybil attacker must therefore fund a separate stake and a separate reputation history for each fake identity, so forging a thousand voices costs a thousand times more, while an honest agent pays once and builds trust for free.
